title: Women and Palm Leaves
paragraphs: Mukilaṉ approached Mullaikkoṭi, when she was coming from the classroom with hands full of the books, received as a prize.
“I am so happy! Congratulations on your winning the prize!” Mukilaṉ said with a smile on his face but he made no attempt to hide his anger.
“Mukilaṉ! Help me with these books. I am unable to carry them.”
“Oh! Do you take me for an aide?” So saying, Mukilaṉ took the bundle of books she received as a prize.
“What Mullai? What sort of a feminist are you? You were advocating male chauvinism!”
“What, me advocating male chauvinism?”
“Exactly! Didn’t you argue in favour of Tolkāppiyam prohibiting women from accompanying men on voyage?”
“Who said that it was Tolkāppiyam’s idea? In the ancient era, such a practice was in vogue. Tolkāppiyar merely reflected it, without concealing anything.”

“I didn’t want to subscribe to that retrogressive principle, which is why I didn’t mention it. But you managed to receive appreciation by holding up views against your own gender. A worst form of female subjugation! Is this how Tolkāppiyam depicts women?”

“These historical facts, lifestyle of people of the yesteryears, their beliefs and their activities based on these beliefs - everything is represented without any concealment by literature. Do you know something, Mukil? The Tolkāppiyar, who refers to the prohibition of women from undertaking voyages, has also spoken about an advantage conferred on women in those days.”
“What was that Mullai?”
“In order to win his beloved by any means, the hero used to ride on a horse made of palmyra leaves in the ancient days.”

“Quite correct! The practice of riding on palmyra horses involved men sitting on horses made of palmyra leaves, going down the street of the town of the heroine and persuading the elders of the town to get him the heroine. The dried leaves of the palmyra would cause bruises all over his body.
In order to save women from experiencing such an excruciating pain, women were prevented from undergoing this process in those days!”
“To realize our love we men underwent maṭalēṟutal; but you women--to achieve the objective of your love...”
“We need not undergo the practice of maṭalēṟutal; instead a mere maṭal (letter) would do the trick.”
“Is that so? Is that so easy? Shall I give it a try?”
“I am sure you mean our marriage invitation!” a blushing Mullaikkoṭi started leaving, taking the books back and holding them tight to her bosom.
“Wish I had been those books!” Though Mukilaṉ didn’t exactly utter these words, his mischievous glance looked like saying so.

> No strand of Akam love behaviour > Does enjoin on the heroine > To ride on the horse of palmyra stems > As it goes contrary to the norms of feminine propriety. > (Poruḷatikāram : Akattiṇai iyal, verse 35).
